topics.titleTr: Hafta Sonunda Claude Code ile SaaS MVP
topics.titleEn: Build a SaaS MVP with Claude Code in a Weekend
topics.angle: how-to + a non-heavy-dev founder ships a real MVP with Claude Code end to end
topics.brief: Story-led build log: a founder ships a scoped SaaS MVP over a weekend with Claude Code. Sections: cutting scope to one core workflow; scaffolding auth, database and billing with the agent; reviewing and testing AI-written code instead of trusting it; deploying; the honest limits (security, edge cases, tech debt) and when to bring in a human dev. Verify: 2026 stat that a large share of production code is AI-generated; agents handle scaffolding well but need review. Sources: 2026 web-dev/AI coding trend reports. End with a weekend timeline and a 'do not skip' safety list. Founder-focused, not an idea list.

topics.titleEn: How to Price AI Features Without Losing Money
topics.angle: guide + price AI features so token costs don't quietly eat your margin
topics.brief: Data-led pricing guide for founders shipping AI features. Sections: mapping token/inference cost per action; flat pricing versus usage credits versus metered; protecting margin with caps, cheaper model tiers and caching; free-tier abuse and how heavy users break flat plans; communicating limits without scaring buyers. Verify: 2026 warning that AI infrastructure is costly and complexity scales fast; smaller models can cut cost sharply. Sources: 2026 bootstrapping/startup trend reports; provider pricing. End with a pricing-model decision table and a margin worksheet.

topics.titleEn: Can You Bootstrap an AI Startup in 2026?
topics.angle: question-driven + whether you can build an AI startup without VC given today's costs
topics.brief: Question-driven, evidence-led take on bootstrapping an AI startup in 2026. Sections: the case for lean (bootstrapped firms show higher early profitability and survival, smaller teams, lower CAC); the real obstacle for AI (infrastructure cost, not headcount); staying thin-wrapper-light versus owning a costly workflow; funding blends (prepayments, revenue-based financing, selective angels); when VC still makes sense. Verify: bootstrapping profitability/survival stats; AI-infra cost caution; avg team size ~4.3. Sources: 2026 bootstrapping trend reports. End with a self-assessment: bootstrap, blend, or raise.

topics.titleTr: Becerini AI ile Urunlesmis Hizmete Cevir
topics.titleEn: Turn Your Skill Into a Productized Service with AI
topics.angle: guide + package a repeatable fixed-scope service and use AI to deliver it profitably
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to building a productized service (fixed scope, fixed price, repeatable delivery) with AI in the workflow. Sections: choosing a painful, repeatable deliverable; scoping and pricing a package versus hourly; a delivery pipeline where AI drafts and you finish; intake, SLAs and boundaries; scaling with templates and a small team before productizing into software. Verify: productized services as a bootstrapper-friendly category; no-code/AI lowering delivery cost. Sources: 2026 startup/solopreneur trend reports. End with a one-page service-spec template. Distinct from selling AI automation to others.

topics.titleTr: Icerik Ureticiler Icin Claude, ChatGPT, Gemini
topics.titleEn: Claude vs ChatGPT vs Gemini for Creators
topics.angle: comparison + which of the big three AI tools fits scripting, captions and ideation
topics.brief: Data-led comparison of Claude, ChatGPT and Gemini for content creators (not developers). Sections: ideation and hooks; long-form scripting and repurposing; captions and platform-native copy; image/asset help and integrations (Gemini in Workspace, ChatGPT plugins, Claude Design); voice consistency and factual reliability; cost for a solo creator. Verify: current model tiers and creator-relevant features of each in mid-2026. Sources: vendor news; creator-tool comparisons. End with a pick-by-workflow table and a cheap starter stack. Creator-audience angle, distinct from developer model comparisons.

topics.titleEn: TikTok's 2026 Algorithm: What Actually Gets Reach
topics.angle: guide + what TikTok's overhauled 2026 ranking rewards and how to earn reach
topics.brief: Question-driven guide to TikTok's overhauled 2026 recommendation system. Sections: the January overhaul and the reported 'authenticity score'; why watch-completion curves, re-watch rate and in-app saves now outweigh raw likes; follower engagement moving to the center; content patterns that fit these signals; what stopped working. Verify: 2026 authenticity-score reporting; completion/re-watch/save weighting. Sources: 2026 TikTok algorithm analyses (OpusClip, Ampfluence). End with a per-video checklist to maximize completion and saves. Distinct from TikTok Shop and cross-platform posting pieces.

topics.titleEn: YouTube Shorts in 2026: Win Attention Depth
topics.angle: how-to + grow on Shorts under the 2026 attention-depth ranking
topics.brief: Question-driven Shorts strategy after YouTube's February 2026 update that prioritizes 'attention depth' over raw views. Sections: what attention depth measures (how much viewers watch and whether they stay on YouTube after); scripting for sustained attention and rewatch; using Community posts and Collab features; funneling Shorts viewers to long-form; measuring session contribution, not just play count. Verify: Feb 2026 Shorts update; attention-depth definition. Sources: 2026 algorithm coverage. End with a Shorts publishing checklist tuned for retention and session lift. Distinct from the Shorts-vs-Reels-vs-TikTok comparison.

topics.angle: contrarian + build a content system that survives constant algorithm changes
topics.brief: Contrarian strategy piece: platforms changed algorithms more in Q1 2026 than in the prior three years, and marketers now rank algorithm volatility as their top operational risk. Sections: why chasing each update is a losing game; owning the audience (email, community, direct); formats and value that travel across platforms; a portfolio approach to channels; metrics that reflect real demand, not reach spikes. Verify: Q1 2026 algorithm-change and top-risk stats. Sources: 2026 social algorithm reports (Stack Influence, Influencers Time). End with an algorithm-resilient content operating system.

topics.titleEn: TanStack Start: A Full-Stack React Alternative
topics.angle: guide + what TanStack Start is and when to choose it over Next.js
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to TanStack Start, the team's full-stack meta-framework built on TanStack Router and Vite. Sections: how it positions against Next.js and Remix; type-safe routing and data loading; SSR and streaming; where the Vite foundation helps DX; migration and maturity caveats in 2026; when Next.js is still the safer pick. Verify: TanStack Start built on Router + Vite; full-stack positioning. Sources: TanStack docs; 2026 React trend reports (LogRocket, eSparkInfo). End with a decision checklist and a minimal starter outline.

topics.titleEn: WebGPU in 2026: GPU Power in the Browser
topics.angle: deep-dive + what WebGPU unlocks and when to reach for it in web apps
topics.brief: Story-led deep-dive on WebGPU in 2026. Sections: what WebGPU is and how it differs from WebGL; browser support status; real use cases (in-browser ML inference, data viz, image/video processing, games); a minimal compute-shader example concept; performance wins and the fallback story for unsupported browsers; when it is overkill. Verify: WebGPU support across major browsers in 2026; on-device inference use case. Sources: MDN WebGPU docs; browser status pages. End with a should-you-use-WebGPU checklist and gotchas.

topics.titleEn: Wiring AI Agents Into Your CI/CD Safely
topics.angle: guide + run coding agents in pipelines with guardrails that prevent runaway changes
topics.brief: Contrarian guide to putting AI coding agents inside CI/CD without letting them run wild. Sections: good jobs for agents (triage, dependency bumps, test generation, first-pass fixes) versus jobs to keep human; sandboxing, least-privilege tokens and no prod write access; requiring human approval and signed commits; cost and rate controls; auditing agent actions and rollback. Verify: 2026 trend of agent guardrails and least-privilege for autonomous tools. Sources: CI/CD and agent-safety guidance; vendor docs. End with a pipeline-integration checklist and a red-lines list.

topics.titleEn: Preview Environments for Every Pull Request
topics.angle: how-to + spin up ephemeral per-PR environments so reviewers test real changes
topics.brief: Field-notes guide to ephemeral preview environments per pull request. Sections: why per-PR environments cut review friction and catch bugs early; approaches (platform-native previews, Kubernetes namespaces, docker-compose on demand); seeding data and stubbing external services; secrets and cost controls; tearing down automatically to avoid sprawl; database branching to isolate schema changes. Verify: preview envs reduce 'works on my machine' and speed review. Sources: platform docs (Vercel/Netlify), GitOps guides. End with a build-vs-buy decision list and a teardown checklist.

topics.titleTr: Bilgi Calisanlari Icin Gunluk AI Is Akislari
topics.titleEn: Daily AI Workflows for Knowledge Workers
topics.angle: how-to + practical daily routines that put ChatGPT, Claude and Gemini to real work
topics.brief: Story-led playbook of daily AI routines for knowledge workers. Sections: inbox and meeting triage; turning notes into drafts and decisions (ChatGPT Work / Claude); research and summarizing with citations you verify; Gemini inside Workspace for docs and sheets; scheduled/recurring tasks; guardrails against over-trusting output and leaking sensitive data. Verify: ChatGPT Work and agent/scheduled-task capabilities; Gemini-in-Workspace features in 2026. Sources: vendor guides; productivity write-ups. End with a copy-and-adapt daily template and a 'never delegate this' list.

topics.titleTr: AI ile Kod Incelemesi: Guven Ama Dogrula
topics.titleEn: AI Code Review: Trust, but Verify
topics.angle: mistakes + use AI code reviewers well and know exactly what they miss
topics.brief: Contrarian guide to AI code review as a complement, not a replacement, for human review. Sections: what AI reviewers catch reliably (style, obvious bugs, boilerplate risks) versus what they miss (intent, architecture, security context, subtle concurrency); false-positive fatigue and how to tune it; keeping humans on design and security-critical paths; integrating AI review in the pipeline without rubber-stamping. Verify: 2026 reality that a large share of code is AI-generated, raising review stakes. Sources: 2026 AI-coding trend reports; review best-practice guides. End with an AI-plus-human review checklist. Distinct from general code-review process posts.
